questions.q: Why would Northbridge generally prefer boto3 over calling AWS's raw REST endpoints with requests?
options: boto3 is the only way to use Python with AWS at all
boto3 handles authentication, retries, and pagination that you'd otherwise have to build by hand
Raw REST calls to AWS are not possible over HTTPS
boto3 is faster at executing Python bytecode
questions.explain: The core advantage of an SDK like boto3 is that it already solves authentication, retry/backoff, and pagination, which you would otherwise reimplement yourself against the raw API.

questions.q: In ec2.describe_volumes(Filters=[{"Name": "status", "Values": ["available"]}]), what does the Filters argument accomplish?
options: It downloads all volumes and filters them in Python afterward
It asks AWS to return only volumes matching the condition, filtering server-side
It deletes every volume with status available
It renames the volumes to 'available'
questions.explain: Filters are passed to AWS and applied server-side, so only matching volumes (here, unattached ones with status 'available') come back in the response.

questions.q: Why use ec2.get_paginator("describe_snapshots") instead of calling describe_snapshots() once and assuming you got everything?
options: Paginators are required by AWS for every single API call
describe_snapshots() cannot be called without a paginator
Many list operations return results across multiple pages, and a paginator walks all of them without you writing a custom token loop
Paginators make the snapshots delete themselves automatically
questions.explain: A paginator automatically follows a provider's pagination tokens across multiple pages, so you don't risk missing results the way a single uncapped call might.

questions.q: In the cleanup example, why does the script tag old volumes with northbridge:status = pending-deletion instead of calling delete_volume immediately?
options: boto3 does not support deleting volumes directly
Tagging is required before any AWS API call will succeed
It gives the infrastructure team a chance to review flagged resources before anything is actually deleted
Tags make volumes cheaper to store
questions.explain: Tagging first and deleting only after review is a safety pattern — it avoids accidentally destroying a resource based on an automated guess that turns out to be wrong.

questions.q: Where does boto3 look to find AWS credentials when you call boto3.client("ec2")?
options: Only from a password typed interactively when the script runs
It refuses to run unless credentials are hardcoded in the script
Environment variables, a shared credentials file, or an IAM role attached to the running machine, checked in order
It generates random credentials automatically
questions.explain: boto3 resolves credentials through a standard chain — environment variables, a credentials file, or an attached IAM role — without you writing manual authentication code.
